title: What happens when you look closer and closer at a fern?
description: A fern leaf is shown, and a branch of it is seen to look like a smaller fern of its own. The video asks what we would keep seeing if we looked closer and closer, and leaves the question open.
teaching_notes: One idea: a shape can be made of smaller copies of itself, again and again. Watch for students who say the branches are just different shapes from the whole leaf.

source: A fern made of smaller ferns
video_script.why: The child meets the chapter's first idea in a real fern, with a question left open.
video_script.substitution: No numbers are used; the fern of the book is the only object.
video_script.anchor: the fern of the book, whose leaves are smaller copies of the whole fern
maths_rules: no number is used in this video
the book says the fern has smaller copies of itself as its leaves, and these have even smaller copies in their sub-leaves
video_script.design: One fern photo, then one drawn fern leaf that is zoomed in twice. Nothing is named or counted.
